page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The CPU includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 937 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a strong contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The i7i.xlarge achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression (34.34 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.1 GB/sec). However, multi-core and memory read bandwidth benchmarks fall into the lower tiers. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance (4390.87) and memory bandwidth read-only small block (343.61 GB/sec) are categorized as weak. Redis SET operations also show lower-tier throughput at 6.18 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput (8.15 GB/sec) and LLM inference speeds for small models remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7i.xlarge offers high resource density by bundling a substantial 937 GB NVMe SSD and 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory with a 4-vCPU footprint. This configuration avoids the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput local data access, though the lower multi-core scaling and read bandwidth present a tradeoff for highly parallelized compute tasks. The instance is best suited for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance and fast local storage, such as relational databases, local caching layers, text processing, and moderate web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 4 vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and a 3.2 GHz clock speed. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it includes 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory and a bundled 937 GB local NVMe SSD. Performance benchmarks highlight exceptional single-core capabilities, with a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 and strong single-threaded compression speeds. However, multi-core scaling and memory read bandwidth are relatively weak, as evidenced by lower-tier stress-ng multi-core and Redis SET operation results. With a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, this Nitro-based instance offers a high-density storage-to-vCPU ratio. It is highly suitable for database operations, text processing, and workloads that benefit from fast local storage and strong single-threaded CPU execution.
